item.title: Dustin Hoffman had a 'terrible experience' making Hollywood classic 'The Graduate'
item.description: Dustin Hoffman reveals in a new essay that he felt "unworthy" and feared being fired every day while filming "The Graduate" with Mike Nichols.
item.content:encoded:
Dustin Hoffman is opening up about the "terrible experience" he had while filming "The Graduate," a film he said "exacerbated all my insecurities from the start."

In a recent essay written for The New Yorker, the 89-year-old actor reflected on his experience making the film, which earned him his first Academy Award nomination and a BAFTA Award win, noting he "felt immediately uncomfortable" and "unworthy" on set.

"Here I was, playing a starring role in a movie by Mike Nichols, who was the director of the moment, but I felt like I had no right to be there," he wrote. "It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life."

He went on to explain that a lot of his time on set was spent wondering if director, Nichols, "was angry at me," because he was either "doing something wrong" or had finally noticed what Hoffman and "everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film."

JOHN GOODMAN ADMITS HE FELT 'FRIGHTENED' AFTER THE SUDDEN FAME HE EXPERIENCED FROM 'ROSEANNE'

The "Rain Man" star felt he was wrong for the part from the start, admitting he "didn't even want to try out for the part," saying he thought "it was obvious" to him after reading the novel the film is based on "that I was all wrong for Benjamin."

"A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was ‘Braddock,’" he said. "Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense." 

Part of what made the experience so bad for Hoffman was his relationship with the director, who he said was "irritable with everyone," and was "frequently sour" on set.

The director's attitude often led to Hoffman feel "that I was about to be fired," as the actor found himself "thinking, I have no f- - -ing idea what I'm doing," while filming some of the most well-known scenes in the movie.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Hoffman also recalled feeling as if the director had a "certain sadism" that was directed mostly towards him.

"There was a scene in which Katharine Ross had to slap me, and he made us do twenty-seven takes. The scene has Benjamin run into Elaine’s room, soaking wet from the rain, to tell her that he’s had an affair with an older woman; within seconds, Elaine realizes the woman is her mother," he said. "Mike just kept telling Katharine to hit me, to hit me harder. Katharine worried she would hurt me, and I told her, ‘I’m O.K. Just don’t hit my ear.’ Unfortunately, she missed a few times. I was dizzy by the end of that day, and Mike didn’t even use the slap in the film."

The next day, Hoffman was scheduled to film a scene underwater, which left him with "blood trickling out of my ear," which later turned out to be a punctured eardrum.

"The Graduate" went on to become one of Hoffman's most well-known films. The movie follows Hoffman's character, Benjamin, a recent college graduate who is struggling to find direction post graduation and is seduced by an older housewife and friend of his parents.

Following its release in 1967, the film was nominated for seven Academy Awards, including best actor for Hoffman and best actress for Anne Bancroft, and ultimately earned Nichols a statue for best director.

item.title: Army student displays hilarious 'communism' sign ahead of game against Air Force
item.description: Army football leads the entire FBS with 342.5 rushing yards per game through eight games in 2026 while throwing just 85 passes all season long.
item.content:encoded:
Army is taking "boots on the ground" to another level, according to their fans.

Fox's Big Noon Kick-off visited West Point ahead of their matchup against rival Air Force Academy . One Army student had a sign that stood out above the rest, making Mark Ingram II take notice and chest bump him. The sign said, "The Forward Pass is Communist."

In case you weren't aware, Army football doesn't just favor running the football, the Black Knights practically treat the forward pass like it's anti-American. They essentially wage war against the forward pass. Army consistently ranks among the nation's leaders in rushing attempts and rushing yards while sitting near the bottom in passing volume.

WHO'S REALLY PLAYED THE BEST THUS FAR THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON?

Rather than airing it out, the Black Knights rely on quarterback keepers, fullback dives and option pitches to grind down opposing defenses, dominate time of possession and keep the clock moving. It's old-school, smash mouth football, which I'm sure gets the boomers to say, "Now this is the football I grew up with!"

Through eight games in 2026, Army leads the entire FBS in rushing yards per game (342.5), piling up 2,740 yards on 431 rushing attempts, an average of 53.9 carries per game. That's a whopping 6.4 yards per carry and 31 rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, the passing game is practically nonexistent. Army ranks 137th out of 138 FBS teams in passing yards per game (69.1) , attempting just 85 passes all season — a measly 10.6 per game, the second-fewest in the country behind Air Force. The Black Knights have thrown for just four touchdowns compared to 31 on the ground, with nearly 83% of their offensive plays coming on rushing attempts.

A LIST OF THE BEST COLLEGE GAMEDAY SIGNS AT LSU DURING SHOW'S 500TH EPISODE

While most college programs are obsessed with throwing the ball all over the field, Army has a much simpler philosophy: Why throw the football when you can run it down your opponent's throat?

Army (5-3) hosts Air Force (6-2) on Saturday at Michie Stadium in West Point, New York, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET. The matchup is part of the annual Commander-in-Chief's Trophy competition, with Army looking for its fourth consecutive victory over the Falcons in a battle featuring the nation's top two rushing offenses.

item.title: IIHF 'taking the necessary steps' to comply with Russia return ruling as Belarus ban remains
item.description: The IIHF says it disagrees with the CAS ruling but is taking steps to allow Russia in the World Junior Championships amid a multinational boycott.
item.content:encoded:
The International Ice Hockey Federation provided updates on Belarusian and Russian athletes in its upcoming world tournaments, including next month's World Junior Championships.

The IIHF announced Saturday that Belarus will not participate, but the federation is "taking the necessary steps required" to comply with the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) ruling to allow Russia to play.

"While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization’s financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the federation said in a statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs, including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey."

The CAS ruled last week that Russian teams can compete in upcoming men's and women's world championships, overturning the International Ice Hockey Federation's (IIHF) decisions to exclude them from its competitions. The World Juniors will be the first tournament affected by the decision.

Hockey Canada and Prime Minister Mark Carney said last week that Russians would not be allowed to play in next month's World Juniors, which will take place in Alberta.

Russia did not compete in Olympic hockey earlier this year, the first since 2014 that had NHL players, nor was it included in the NHL's 4 Nations Face-Off. Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, four days after Olympic competition ended that year.

Vladimir Putin put out a statement through the state-run Russian outlet TASS calling out organizations that are preventing Russian athletes from competing for their country.

HOCKEY GREAT WAYNE GRETZKY DEFENDS RELATIONSHIP WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP AND SPEAKS ON RUSSIAN HOCKEY BAN

"Unfortunately, they have not honored the commitments they once made, and they continue to enforce restrictions against Russian sports that are not based on law, but are instead highly politicized," Putin said, via translation. "This constitutes a clear and gross violation of the law and of judicial rulings — and, by extension, a violation of the very institutions of democracy. That is precisely how this should be interpreted."

Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia and Denmark came out with statements signing up for a boycott of games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. Germany, the host of the 2027 men's world championships, also suggested backing out if Russia was allowed to play.

STRAUSS, a workwear company that is a top sponsor of the world championships next year, threatened to walk away after Finland announced Monday it was rallying other nations to refuse to play Russia.

If Russia makes the trip next month, it will be its first time playing in the World Juniors since 2021. It has not won gold since 2011.

item.title: Urgent travel alert as nationwide strike threatens widespread disruption and delays
item.description: Spain's 24-hour nationwide strike on Nov. 11 could disrupt flights, trains and Barcelona metro service as unions protest the housing crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Travelers heading to Spain this coming week are being urged to check flight and train plans ahead of a 24-hour nationwide strike.

Spain’s two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, have called a 24-hour nationwide strike for Nov. 11 over the housing crisis, The Independent reported. The U.S. Embassy says workers across sectors, including transportation and hospitality, have been called to participate.

Flights, trains and local transit could face disruptions, with demonstrations expected in major cities, though not all specific service interruptions have been confirmed.

AMERICANS WARNED OF VIOLENT PROTESTS AS MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATION FACES SHUTDOWN THREAT

Demonstrations including picket lines may also prompt last-minute closures, cancellations, roadblocks and an increased police presence, according to an alert from the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Spain and Andorra. Shops, restaurants, museums and pharmacies may also close, according to the advisory.

"Demonstrations, both planned and spontaneous, will occur throughout the country," it read. "Even protests, demonstrations, and gatherings intended to be peaceful can escalate quickly or have the potential to turn violent."

FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY

Some details on local interruptions are already available, according to the government of Catalonia's website.

In Catalonia, public transportation — including Barcelona’s metro, buses and regional rail — is set to run at 25% of normal service during morning and evening peak periods: 6:30 to 9:30 a.m. and 4:30 to 9 p.m.

CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE

The bus linking Barcelona and its airport is scheduled to operate at 50% of normal service. Outside the peak windows, no minimum service level has been set for passenger transportation, though that does not necessarily mean all service will stop.

Separately, Catalonia’s commuter and regional rail services will operate at 66% of normal service during peak hours and 33% the rest of the day on Nov. 10 and 12 amid the Renfe train-driver strikes.

ANGRY LOCALS BLOCK FAMOUS BEACH AS MASS TOURISM PROTESTS ESCALATE AT VACATION HOT SPOT

The strike’s effect on individual flights, trains and local services may vary. Travelers should check directly with their airline, train company and local transit operator for updates, and allow extra time to reach airports and stations.

The embassy also advises U.S. citizens to avoid demonstrations and crowds, monitor local news and follow instructions from police and local authorities.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The walkout comes amid demonstrations over housing affordability. One of the major unions said its call seeks urgent action on the housing crisis, along with better wages and labor and social protections.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Recent demonstrations and labor actions across Spain in recent weeks have highlighted several other issues, including rising rents and short-term rentals, calls to restrict tourism in Mallorca and Ibiza, and potential pay cuts for Barcelona port workers, whose protest temporarily blocked access to cruise terminals.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Recent protests elsewhere in Europe have reflected varied local grievances, including housing costs, the cost of living and pressure on public services, according to reports, though they are not necessarily connected to Spain’s strike.

Fox News Digital’s Kelly McGreal, Jessica Mekles, Andrea Margolis, Brittany Miller, Ashley J. DiMella and Teresa Mull contributed reporting.

item.title: Melania Trump secures $7.2M for foster care scholarships at LSU ahead of Alabama showdown
item.description: Melania Trump unveiled a $7.2 million scholarship endowment at LSU for foster care youth before receiving a custom jersey and football tribute.
item.content:encoded:
BATON ROUGE, La. — First lady Melania Trump announced a $7.2 million scholarship endowment at Louisiana State University (LSU) on Saturday, delivering a message of hope to young Americans who have experienced foster care before receiving a special football tribute ahead of the Tigers' rivalry showdown against Alabama.

Trump wore a Dalma suede bomber jacket by Nour Hammour, paired with an Adam Lippes skirt and Manolo Blahnik BB pumps for the occasion, blending her signature polished style with a more relaxed look suited to a college football weekend.

The first lady's visit unfolded against a distinctly LSU backdrop, with purple-and-gold tailgating crowds lining the motorcade route and a massive American flag hanging above the stage inside Patrick F. Taylor Hall. 

LSU cheerleaders flanked Trump during her remarks, and the Tiger mascot presented her with both scholarship checks while wearing a signature "Be Best" T-shirt.

MELANIA TRUMP CHALLENGES CONGRESS TO MAKE HER FOSTER CARE EXECUTIVE ORDER PERMANENT LAW: 'THEIR BIRTHRIGHT'

There, university officials, donors and students gathered for an announcement supporting young Americans who have experienced foster care through Trump's "Fostering the Future" initiative.

"This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation, and a chance to build a wonderful life," Trump told attendees.

The permanent endowment includes a $5 million commitment from MMR Group, led by LSU alumnus James B. "Pepper" Rutland, and an additional $2.2 million raised from 75 LSU Foundation donors.

LSU Foundation President and CEO Krista Raney said the contributions had brought the scholarship fund to "more than $7.2 million and growing."

LSU President Wade Rousse said the $5 million leadership gift is expected to generate approximately $200,000 annually, helping students cover tuition, fees, books and room and board.

ED ORGERON-LANE KIFFIN PAIRING ALREADY PAYING DIVIDENDS FOR LSU TIGERS DURING PIVOTAL RECRUITING WEEKEND

"At LSU, we believe talent is everywhere, but we understand that opportunity is not," Rousse said.

The university also embraced the occasion with several football-themed gifts for the first lady.

Trump received a custom purple-and-gold LSU jersey bearing the name "MELANIA" and the number 14, along with a Tigers helmet featuring her BE BEST Fostering the Future logo.

Former LSU coach Ed Orgeron, known to fans as Coach O, joined the presentation with a specially designed commemorative football created by Big Game USA, a company owned by LSU alumnus Chris Calandra.

The initiative extended beyond the ceremony, with special patches on LSU players' jerseys, helmet decals, cheerleader uniforms, mascot attire and commemorative fan towels, according to the White House.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST

Southeastern Conference officials also agreed to use a special Melania Trump challenge coin for the game's official coin toss.

The legendary LSU-Alabama rivalry even found its way into the scholarship announcement.

After Trump revealed that LSU has 14 Fostering the Future scholars compared with Alabama's nine, Raney offered a lighthearted observation.

"Mrs. Trump, what I heard you say is that LSU has 14 scholarship recipients and Alabama has nine," Raney said. "So I think that means we've already won the first point."

Trump told attendees that 26 universities nationwide are supporting 100 Fostering the Future scholars this semester.

"While most eyes will be on the athletes today, I encourage you to recognize LSU's Fostering the Future scholars, who are just as remarkable," she said.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, Louisiana first lady Sharon Landry and House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., were among those in attendance.

Trump also received a handcrafted wooden bowl made from a fallen limb of one of LSU's historic oak trees, a gift symbolizing the lasting impact of the scholarship initiative.

Fostering the Future, launched in 2021 as part of Trump's BE BEST initiative, seeks to expand educational opportunities for young people who have experienced foster care.

"A great education does more than prepare someone for work life," Trump said. "It gives something no one can ever take away."

She closed with an encouraging message to scholarship recipients.

"To the Fostering the Future scholars here today, and throughout America: I see you. I believe in you. And I will keep working to create new opportunities with you," she said.

item.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Trump says he offered UFC CEO Dana White press secretary job
item.description: President Donald Trump proposed UFC CEO Dana White as White House press secretary in a Truth Social post, naming MMA fighters as assistants.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Saturday he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House press secretary job, proposing a team of mixed martial arts stars to help defend his administration against political opponents.

Shortly after Trump published his post, White shared a photo on his Instagram Story of himself standing at the White House press podium with the caption, "On to the next chapter." He also shared Trump’s Truth Social post announcing the offer.

The Nov. 7 Truth Social post paired the proposed offer with a roster of fighters and an image collage. It did not establish that White had accepted the position, and it was not immediately clear whether Trump intended the proposal seriously.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote.

DANA WHITE SAYS 'I DON'T GIVE A S---' IF TRUMP FRIENDSHIP COSTS HIM BUSINESS, 250TH EVENT WAS TRUMP'S IDEA

The president named Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and Amanda Nunes as prospective assistants, while acknowledging that some were not American. He also listed "Kayla Harris," apparently referring to UFC fighter and two-time Olympic judo gold medalist Kayla Harrison.

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump added.

The post comes amid turnover in the White House’s senior ranks and weeks after the departure of Trump’s most recent press secretary.

Fox News Digital reported Oct. 16 that Katie Zacharia was leaving the position following her debut. Trump had announced her selection Oct. 9 to succeed Karoline Leavitt, who left in August. ABC News reported that Zacharia began work Oct. 12 and was transitioning out of the role that Friday.

Asked Oct. 23 about finding another press secretary, Trump told reporters, "No, nothing much. We’re in no rush."

Separately, the White House announced Friday that Stephen Miller would succeed Susie Wiles as chief of staff. That announcement confirmed a personnel change; Trump’s Saturday appeal to White left the proposed press secretary arrangement unresolved.

UFC'S DANA WHITE SAYS 'YOU'D BE SHOCKED' TO LEARN WHO ACTUALLY SUPPORTS TRUMP IN THE SHADOWS

White and Trump have a relationship stretching back decades, rooted partly in Trump’s support for UFC when the promotion was working to establish itself.

Trump hosted UFC events in Atlantic City as early as 2001, according to Sports Business Journal. White later became a prominent supporter of Trump’s presidential campaigns and spoke during his 2024 election-night victory celebration.

White also introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, describing their long friendship and praising Trump’s resilience.

Their relationship carried into Trump’s second term. The president attended UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn on June 14, 2026. Official White House photographs documented Trump and White walking through the building together to attend the event.

White has previously downplayed the prospect of entering politics himself.

"I have no personal political aspirations," he told Sports Business Journal in November 2024 when asked about a potential role in Trump’s incoming administration.

That statement preceded Saturday’s post by two years and does not establish White’s response to the latest proposal.

OutKick has reached out to the White House and UFC for comment.

item.title: Liberal podcasters apologize after laughing at joke about digging up Charlie Kirk's body
item.description: Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan laughed on the "I've Had It" podcast over a post referencing Charlie Kirk's death, sparking outrage.
item.content:encoded:
Podcasters Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan drew criticism from political commentators after laughing at a social media post about exhuming the body of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. The two issued an apology on Saturday. 

During Thursday's episode of Welch's "I've Had It" podcast, the two women laughed as they read social media reactions to Democrats' victories in the 2026 midterm elections. Several posts mocked conservative positions on issues including abortion, vaccines and LGBTQ+ policies.

"Somebody posted, ‘I don’t care if you celibate or abstinent. Grab the nearest person available and do your worst. Abortion’s on me,’" Welch said, reading from the social media posts.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

The pair continued to laugh as they read other social media reactions mocking Republicans following the party's midterm election losses.

"You can't even fathom the pronouns we're going to invent," Welch read while laughing. "You can't even pronounce them."

The podcast host praised the writers of the various posts, calling the jokesters "patriots" and insisting that "these people make me patriotic."

Welch further broke out into laughter while reading another post aloud: "We're digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again."

'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL

On Saturday, the two hosts apologized via a post on Instagram.

"On Thursday’s show, we laughed at a joke about Charlie Kirk. It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize," the statement read. "Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence. We’ve long supported common-sense gun safety reform." 

"To that end, we’ve made a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in America," the statement continued. "We’ll keep using our platforms to fight for the safety of all Americans."

During Thursday's episode, after laughing at the post, the hosts said, "No comment," before asserting without presenting evidence that Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Kirk, supported President Donald Trump.

DEMOCRATIC STUDENT GROUP TO PROTEST CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL AT CAMPUS WHERE HE WAS KILLED

"Other than he was shot by somebody that was super MAGA," Sullivan said.

"He was shot by a MAGA person," Welch said, adding, "White person, White MAGA family."

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

While Robinson and his family lived in Utah’s Washington County, a deep red county where 75% of residents voted to send President Donald Trump back to the White House, Fox News Digital previously reported that Utah Voter Registration records showed that Robinson is unaffiliated with a political party and did not vote in the past two general elections.

Several commentators criticized the hosts' remarks on social media.

PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST

"In all of their hatred and blood thirst, these ghouls seriously consider themselves morally superior to you," conservative activist Riley Gaines said in an X post.

"They will celebrate your death, laugh uncontrollably, and still be fully convinced they're the 'good guys,'" influencer Collin Rugg posted.

Media Research Center President David Bozell also criticized the hosts, telling Fox News Digital, "If Madison Ave. would stop sponsoring gutter trash, gutter trash would go out of business."

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff also criticized Welch and Sullivan's remarks.

BOBBY BURACK: ONLINE HATE IS WINNING, FROM PAT MCAFEE TO EVERYDAY AMERICANS AND YOUNG CHILDREN

"As a Democrat, it is frustrating to watch Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan get treated like voices for the Democratic Party when so much of their own brand is railing against Democrats," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "Have either of them persuaded a single person to vote for a Democrat?"

"Then, after Democrats just delivered historic wins and a massive blue wave, they say something this offensive and irresponsible and suddenly the story is about them instead," he added. "They are not helping Democrats. They are hijacking the attention Democrats actually earned at the ballot box."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Welch and Sullivan did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Deirdre Heavey contributed to this report.

item.title: Daniel Jones trade buzz grows as Colts open door to offers ahead of NFL deadline: report
item.description: Daniel Jones has drawn trade interest from multiple NFL teams, with the Indianapolis Colts willing to listen to offers before the Nov. 10 deadline.
item.content:encoded:
It appears truly nobody is untouchable on the Indianapolis Colts prior to the NFL trade deadline.

The Colts have been engaged in trade discussions with players like Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs after dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner to kick off what many expect to be a wild trade deadline period.

But quarterback Daniel Jones is someone they’re willing to at least listen to trade offers on now, according to ESPN and NFL Network.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Colts have reportedly received calls from multiple teams asking if Jones is available. They’ve at least been willing to hear out those teams, as Jones prepares to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 9.

Among those teams were the Baltimore Ravens, who are probably out of the running now that they reached an agreement with the Arizona Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett.

There is also speculation that the Minnesota Vikings, who have struggled offensively despite a 6-1 record, could be calling the Colts and owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon for Jones’ services. He has a history with Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell, who he worked with after the New York Giants released him midway through his first contract extension.

Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract extension worth up to $100 million in March 2026, with the Colts showing him loyalty despite tearing his Achilles in Week 14 last season.

The Colts were one of the best teams in the NFL, but once Jones’ injury knocked him out for the season, Indianapolis failed to find a viable replacement, including the hope Philip Rivers could get the job done by bringing him out of retirement.

The Vikings seem to be a consistent quarterback away from a true run to the Super Bowl given their defense, led by coordinator Brian Flores, has been one of the most suffocating units in the league thus far. Kyler Murray, whom the Vikings quickly made QB1, has not delivered that consistent play, and it O’Connell will hope Wentz can do so this week against the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football."

After shipping out Nelson and Buckner, the Colts haven’t found the right deal for them to part ways with other high-caliber players. The Nov. 10 deadline at 4 p.m. ET will be telling.

As for Jones, head coach Shane Steichen believes he is the man for the job in Indianapolis, and said he "gives us the best chance to win right now." But if the Colts are rebuilding, looking to sell off intriguing pieces for draft capital and more, winning right now might not be the mindset of the organization.

It’s all Zayn ever really wanted from his former Bloodline brother. It’s what he’s wanted from the WWE Universe and the rest of the locker room on SmackDown. item.title: Arch Manning, Texas escape Missouri after wild officiating controversy sends SEC showdown into chaos
item.description: Texas Longhorns escaped Columbia after Arch Manning's controversial fumble ruling and a chaotic SEC officiating crew left Missouri fans stunned.
item.content:encoded:
The argument of whether Texas would make the college football playoff if it were to lose another game this season will have to wait another week.

But, that doesn’t mean the controversy surrounding this Longhorns squad is going away any time soon after the 34-20 win over Missouri.

Did SEC officials get together before the game and decide that pure chaos was on the agenda for this showdown at Missouri?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Besides the fact that there were multiple calls that went against Missouri, some reasonable, I don't think we've seen this much madness in one football game this season.

Everything came to a head in the third quarter, as Arch Manning was hit from behind while trying to also complete a pass. The Texas quarterback was obviously trying to pass the football, while at the same time a Missouri defender got his hand on the ball.

The problem was that Manning's arm was moving forward, even with the ball tipped by a Missouri defender. Then, as the ball laid on the ground 12 yards ahead of the the line of scrimmage, a Texas receiver picked up the football, while trying to snag it before a Missouri defender fell on the ball.

While a befuddled broadcast crew and those reacting on social media complained, Arch Manning dropped a dime just two plays later for the Texas touchdown that tied the game at 20-20.

This was just one example that created plenty of confusion for viewers at home, while the home Missouri crowd was left stunned.

Maybe this is one of those examples of how anyone in the SEC can be beaten on any given Saturday. DID WE CREATE A MONSTER? ARCH MANNING’S ‘AW SHUCKS’ PERSONA IS GONE BEFORE MUST-WIN OLE MISS GAME

item.title: Government witness says Shohei Ohtani scandal dried up inside betting info on Emmanuel Clase's pitches
item.description: A government witness admitted to winning thousands betting on Emmanuel Clase's pitch speeds using inside tips shared through an Uber driver group chat.
item.content:encoded:
As the Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz federal trial continued on Friday in New York, a government witness added a very interesting wrinkle to the case during his testimony.

Luis de Aza Baez admitted to placing dozens of bets, and winning thousands, by wagering on the speed Clase’s pitch came across home plate during the 2023 MLB season. He said he placed the bets "because I had inside information," per ESPN.

Clase has been accused of rigging 18 pitches across three seasons in conspiracy with bettors.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

However, de Aza Baez also noted that when he asked about Clase’s pitches the following season, there was a hiccup.

"What was going on with [Shohei] Ohtani, there was no more information like that," de Aza Baez said in his testimony.

In March 2024, Ohtani wasn’t facing accusations like Clase and Ortiz, but he faced scrutiny after millions had been sent from his bank account to an illegal bookmaking operation. But Ippei Mizuhara, his longtime interpreter, pleaded guilty to stealing almost $17 million from Ohtani to pay off gambling debts.

MLB CATCHER WHO WAS BEHIND PLATE FOR ALLEGED RIGGED PITCHES TESTIFIES IN GUARDIANS PITCHERS' GAMBLING CASE

Mizuhara is currently in prison, while Ohtani was cleared of any wrongdoing in the case.

De Aza Baez was working as an Uber driver at the time, and he had a group chat called "Uber Inc.," where Enoc Pena, an associate of Clase, would send tips in 2023, according to his testimony. Pena was the one who started the chat with the men who worked for Uber in the Massachusetts area.

Prosecutors showed a text message screenshot Clase allegedly had sent to Pena on Sept. 30, 2023, when the Cleveland Guardians were set to face the Detroit Tigers. Clase and Pena spoke about "killing the first two chickens," which was code to bet on a pitch against the third batter, granted Clase came in the game and got the first two outs. He never entered the contest in the 8-0 Detroit victory.

Clase’s defense team argued the text message was misconstrued, as roosters and chickens in such talks with Pena often refer to cockfighting, which is legal in his native Dominican Republic.

De Aza Baez and Clase became friends, and were seen in a video at a relative’s house playing dominoes on a Boston Red Sox-logoed table. However, de Aza Baez testified he never received direct information about pitches from Clase – only Pena.

De Aza Baez said he "almost always" won when Pena dropped the tip to him, and though there were no official cuts to be handed out, he gave him some money after winning the bet.

Clase and Ortiz, also an ex-Guardians pitcher have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy of wire and honor services fraud, sports bribery and money laundering.

"Our defense is the same today as it was in opening: This is a case about big talk and small bets," Vásquez's attorney Todd Spodek told ESPN following the hearing on Friday. "We're confident leaving that judgment to the jury."

De Aza Baez agreed with the federal government to forfeit $69,000 won on bets involving Clase, saying he would "tell the truth" in exchange for dropping the wire fraud charge in the case.

Prior to De Aza Baez’s testimony, former Guardians catcher Bo Naylor, who was behind the plate for the allegedly rigged pitches by both Clase and Ortiz, testified on Thursday in New York.

He said he appeared to call one of the allegedly rigged pitches that were shown to him on a screen inside the courtroom, saying that a slider away to St. Louis Cardinals’ Pedro Pages was a weakness. He also noted he was unaware bettors could even wager on specific pitches.

Attorneys elicited from Naylor that he had frequently seen Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room. Prosecutors have alleged that Clase sometimes broke Major League Baseball rules by communicating with gamblers during games.

Bettors allegedly won $400,000 from betting platforms on pitches thrown by Clase between 2023 and 2025. Ortiz allegedly joined the scheme in June 2025.

Clase was one of baseball’s best closers, pitching to a 1.21 ERA in his 2024 season, finishing third in AL Cy Young voting. But his ERA ballooned to 3.80 in 2025 by the time he was investigated.

item.title: No 3 Utah remains undefeated with thrilling win over No 9 BYU behind Heisman finalist Devon Dampier's epic day
item.description: Utah defeated BYU 28-20 in the Holy War as quarterback Devon Dampier was fantastic in the win, firmly planting himself in the Heisman conversation.
item.content:encoded:
The Holy War may have kicked off early, but both Utah and BYU were up to the task and delivered an instant classic.

No. 3 Utah (9-0) defeated No. 9 BYU 28-20 on Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium in a thrilling game that had major College Football Playoff and Big 12 championship implications. Utes quarterback Devon Dampier was outstanding in the win and vaulted himself into the Heisman Trophy conversation. Dampier was 14 of 26 for 177 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 87 yards and two touchdowns.

For Utah, the win was its 15th straight, the longest active winning streak in college football, and also snapped a three-game losing streak to BYU. The Utes remain undefeated and are in the driver's seat to make the Big 12 championship game and are all but assured to make the College Football Playoff.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

With the loss, BYU was dealt a crushing blow that threatened its College Football Playoff and Big 12 championship game hopes.

The Holy War began at 10:00 a.m. local time, and Utah was ready.

The Utes scored the first touchdown of the game at 10:10 a.m. local time, just 1:15 into the first quarter. Quarterback Devon Dampier scored on a 22-yard run to put the Utes up 7-0 early. It was their eighth opening touchdown drive of the season.

Utah then forced a BYU three-and-out and went right back down the field immediately. Dampier found wide receiver Braden Pegan wide open over the middle of the field, and the pair connected for a 46-yard touchdown to put Utah up 14-0.

In less than five minutes, Utah was up by two scores. It was their first double-digit lead over BYU since 2019. It looked like the 104th edition of the Holy War might be a rout, but BYU had other plans, as the Cougars dominated the rest of the first half.

BYU's comeback began with back-to-back field goals, cutting the lead to 14-6 before finally finding the end zone. On the first play of the drive, Bear Bachmeier found a streaking Legend Glasker for a 75-yard touchdown to cut the lead to 14-13.

Utah's lead would not last long, as Pegan fumbled the ball away at midfield on the ensuing possession. BYU's offense kept the pressure on, scoring off the fumble with running back LJ Martin rushing for a 4-yard touchdown to put the Cougars up 20-14.

It looked like BYU’s momentum was going to carry all the way into halftime. Dampier tried to escape the pocket deep in his own end of the field but got the ball punched out from behind by BYU defensive end Bodie Schoonover, and BYU recovered.

However, the Utah defense finally stood tall . Bachmeier, trying to capitalize on the fumble, overthrew his receiver, and defensive back James Chenault Jr. juggled the ball and came up with the crucial interception.

While Utah wasn’t able to score after the interception, the Utes prevented BYU from extending its lead. Utah's offense had just 32 yards and two fumbles on their final six possessions of the first half after scoring on their first two drives.

BYU got the ball first in the third quarter, but it was Utah who made the first impact play of the second half. Defensive end Lance Holtzclaw dropped into coverage and picked off Bachmeier.

However, Utah's offensive futility continued. On fourth-and-1 at midfield, Utah's offense dialed up a trick play as wide receiver Creed Whittemore threw deep to Dampier, and the quarterback hauled it in for a 29-yard gain.

It looked like Utah was going to take advantage and score a touchdown after the incredible conversion, but Whittemore had the ball go through his hands in the end zone on third down. It looked like Utah was going to walk away with a field goal, but kicker Dillon Curtis missed the 29-yard attempt, as BYU held its 20-14 lead.

Utah's defense got another stop against BYU, and the Utes' offense finally snapped out of its funk. Pegan caught his second touchdown of the game on a 14-yard fade, as Dampier threw a great pass. The Utes took their first lead since the first quarter with the extra point, putting them up 21-20 late in the third quarter.

After the touchdown, momentum started to build for Utah . The Utes stopped BYU on the ensuing possession, and the offense once again marched down the field behind Dampier's rushing attack .

However, on third-and-7 from the BYU 18-yard line, Utah took its first timeout of the half. While the Utes didn't complete the pass, BYU cornerback Jayven Williams committed a pass-interference penalty to extend the drive.

Dampier once again played the hero, running in his second touchdown of the game on third-and-goal from the 3-yard line. Curtis nailed the extra point , putting Utah up 28-20.

It looked like BYU was going to score a touchdown and maybe even tie the game on the following drive, but Utah's defense came up with its biggest play of the day. On third-and-goal from the Utah 2-yard line, Bachmeier dropped back to pass and tried to throw a slant, but linebacker Trey Reynolds jumped the route and intercepted the ball, ending the scoring threat.

BYU had to burn all of their timeouts, but they were able to get the ball back with under a minute left at the game after stopping Utah. Utah punter Orion Phillips' punt was poor, going just 18 yards, and BYU started the drive on their own 48-yard line.

However, with Bachmeier forced to be desperate with the clock winding down, he heaved it to the end zone and was picked off for the fourth time in the game by safety Nate Ritchie to seal the Utah win.

Bachmeier threw three interceptions against Utah after throwing just four all season entering the game. He completed 21 of 35 passes for 272 yards with one touchdown and four interceptions with 59 rushing yards.

Utah will look to keep its undefeated season alive when it plays No. 22 Arizona next Saturday. BYU will look to bounce back when it plays Baylor next week.

item.title: Member of largest teachers union in US claims org is 'no longer focused on children,' only 'political power'
item.description: A 26-year NEA and California Teachers Association member says unions abandoned classroom instruction to focus on political power and activism.
item.content:encoded:
A long-serving member of the National Education Association (NEA) and the California Teachers Association (CTA) told Fox News Digital that major teachers unions have abandoned instructional quality to focus almost exclusively on accumulating political power.

"It's all about power," said Michael Greer, a special education teacher who spent 26 years as a CTA and NEA member. "In California, the California Teachers Association is the most powerful lobbying group in the state, which also transfers into the national union."

Greer — a retired educator with two decades of classroom experience who previously served as a local CTA chapter president and as a member of the Del Norte County Unified School District Board of Trustees — said the unions’ core priorities have fundamentally shifted since he entered public education.

PRO-TRUMP GROUP LEADS NEW COALITION TO UNDERCUT TEACHERS UNIONS

"When I first became a union president, it was about the teachers. We were focused on helping educators become better at what they do — helping them teach reading, math, and science," Greer explained, noting that union-sponsored conferences used to feature practical instructional workshops and classroom training. "We took those programs back and taught our colleagues how to implement them. That has changed completely."

Greer’s remarks follow independent analyses revealing that the nation's two largest teachers unions — the NEA and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) — have directed hundreds of millions of dollars toward political activism, lobbying, and progressive advocacy groups over the last decade.

According to an investigation by the North American Values Institute (NAVI), an education watchdog tracking ideological activism, the NEA spent at least $547 million on political activity and advocacy between fiscal years 2016 and 2025. That total includes $458.9 million officially designated as political and lobbying expenditures, along with $88.2 million in direct contributions to progressive organizations. During the same period, the AFT reported $383.2 million in political activity and lobbying, NAVI found.

A separate report from Parents Defending Education found that national teachers unions have funneled over $660 million to left-wing political groups and causes since 2015. When state and local affiliates are included, total union political spending tops $1 billion.

NATION’S LARGEST TEACHERS UNION UNDER FIRE AS CONTROVERSIAL AGENDA PUTS CENTURY-OLD FEDERAL CHARTER AT RISK

According to the Parents Defending Education report, those contributions went to major Democratic-aligned political action committees — including the Senate Majority PAC and House Majority PAC — as well as progressive groups like the State Engagement Fund (over $60 million) and the For Our Future Action Fund (over $40 million).

Greer argued that this political spending has altered what unions expect from their members.

"What it has changed to is teaching teachers how to become union members, how to go on strike, and how to gain social justice power," Greer told Fox News Digital. "We got away from teaching teachers how to teach and moved toward teaching them how to change the social system."

The union emphasis on political activism comes amid persistent declines in student academic achievement. Federal education officials recently noted that national assessment data shows only about three in 10 students are proficient in math and reading, despite more than $3 trillion in federal taxpayer funding spent since the U.S. Department of Education was created in 1979.

JONATHAN TURLEY: CHICAGO SCHOOLS REWARD PROTEST WHILE STUDENTS CAN'T READ

Greer, who also serves as chair of the Del Norte County Republican Party, acknowledged that the CTA maintains relationships across party lines at the state level — including funding travel for teachers of both major political parties to attend state political conventions.

"The CTA actually funds teachers to attend both the state Republican and Democratic conventions," Greer said. "They will cover up to $800 for hotel and transportation, so teachers can participate."

However, Greer said his vocal opposition to the union’s shift from classroom instruction to political activism has made him a rare ideological outlier within the organization.

"That's why I'm known as one of the ‘bad boys’ in California education," Greer said. "I’ve spoken out because they aren't helping teachers on the ground floor where instruction actually happens — they are helping themselves gain the power to alter laws and regulations."

MCMAHON CALLS FOR 'RESET' OF EDUCATION AFTER US SPENT $3 TRILLION AND STILL SAW READING SCORES DECLINE

"I’ve seen it as a school board member, and I’ve seen it as an NEA-CTA delegate at national conferences," Greer added. "They are no longer focused on children and what they are learning. It’s about what teachers can do for political power, and that’s where my problem lies as I watch my union dues being spent."

Fox News Digital reached out to the National Education Association and the California Teachers Association for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Certain sleep habits could offer clues to hidden type of depression, scientists say
item.description: A study of over 11,000 Australian adults links specific sleep habits and circadian rhythm disruptions to a newly proposed subtype of depression.
item.content:encoded:
A person's sleep habits may help identify a newly proposed subtype of depression linked to the body's internal clock.

In a study of 11,380 Australian adults with a history of depression, about 23% met researchers' criteria for what they called "circadian depression."

The profile included at least three of six features: being an evening person, waking up feeling very tired, sleeping longer during the worst periods of depression, experiencing seasonal changes, having a later midpoint between falling asleep and waking up, and experiencing "social jetlag," a large shift in sleep timing between workdays and days off.

The seasonal changes could involve sleep, mood, activity, appetite, weight or energy.

THE DAYTIME HABIT THAT COULD TRANSFORM YOUR SLEEP, ACCORDING TO NEW STUDY

The study, published on Oct. 20 in The British Journal of Psychiatry, could eventually help guide more personalized care for patients with depression, according to the researchers.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them," first author Emiliana Tonini, Ph.D., from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Centre, said in a statement.

The label, however, is not a formal diagnosis and needs independent replication and further study, the researchers noted.

People in the circadian group reported an earlier onset of depression and more severe symptoms than those who did not meet the criteria. They were also more likely to report weight gain during depressive episodes.

They also reported poorer responses and more side effects with two common classes of antidepressants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs).

POPULAR SLEEP AIDS BEFORE SURGERY COULD PREVENT PAINKILLER DEPENDENCE LATER

Participants reported how well their medications worked, but the study did not explain why some were less effective and did not test treatments aimed at adjusting the body’s internal clock. 

Researchers said light exposure, regular sleep schedules and melatonin-related approaches warrant further study.

Dr. Ian Hickie, a study co-author and professor of psychiatry at the University of Sydney, said the proposed profile "cuts across existing historic subtypes" of depression, most commonly atypical and bipolar depression, because they share features such as low energy and oversleeping.

COMMON GYM SUPPLEMENT COULD HELP FIGHT DEPRESSION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

Atypical depression can also involve weight gain, while bipolar depression refers to depressive episodes in people with bipolar disorder, which also involves periods of unusually elevated or irritable mood and increased energy.

"We define circadian only by sleep-wake and circadian features," Hickie told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

For some people with this profile, Hickie said sleep-wake disruption may be more than a symptom of depression. "This type of circadian disturbance is not simply a consequence, but the underlying cause," he wrote.

The study itself, however, could not establish whether body-clock disruption caused depression or resulted from it.

Staying up late or having trouble waking does not necessarily indicate depression. Participants had already reported depression, which in some cases was severe, recurring or long-lasting.

Participants in the circadian group also reported more manic-like experiences. John Puls, a psychotherapist and adjunct professor at Florida Atlantic University, said those symptoms could help explain their reported response to antidepressants.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"SSRIs are not meant to treat these more significant mental health symptoms that go far beyond depressive symptoms," Puls, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "In fact, some SSRIs can actually worsen manic symptoms, which lead to poor sleep."

There were several limitations to the study, the researchers acknowledged. 

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Participants reported their own sleep patterns and treatment experiences, and the cross-sectional analysis didn't show whether sleep disruption preceded or followed depressive symptoms.

All participants were of European ancestry, so the findings may not apply to other populations.

Jillian Amodio, a Maryland-based psychotherapist and founder of Moms For Mental Health, cautioned against using the findings as "a benchmark for treating each person in the same way."

"Biological, environmental, social and psychological factors all need to be accounted for," Amodio, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

Researchers should examine more populations, including people who work night shifts, and account for differences in time zones and seasons, according to Amodio.

The study was led by researchers at the University of Sydney and QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute, with co-authors from institutions in Australia, the U.K. and the U.S.

item.title: Pro-trans activists hold rally against Washington state ballot initiative to protect girls sports
item.description: Protesters marched through Seattle Thursday after Washington voters approved Initiative 638 barring biological males from girls' K-12 sports.
item.content:encoded:
Transgender-rights supporters marched through downtown Seattle Thursday after Washington voters approved a measure barring biological males from girls’ K–12 interscholastic sports, setting up a potential court battle over the new restrictions.

Demonstrators gathered at Westlake Park before marching toward Pike Place Market, according to KUOW. The protest followed the passage of Initiative 638, which also requires students seeking to compete in girls’ sports to provide medical verification of their biological sex.

The measure had 56.8% support in returns reported Thursday by FOX 13 Seattle. The Associated Press called its passage Wednesday evening, with ballots still being counted.

WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS APPEAR TO PASS FIRST-EVER BALLOT MEASURE SEPARATING BOYS AND GIRLS SPORTS

"I was kind of expecting it, but it was still devastating nonetheless," Evan Gortner of Gender Equity Movement, which organized the protest, told KUOW.

Marchers chanted, "638 is trans hate." Some attendees also criticized Democratic leaders for not doing more to defeat the initiative.

The result delivered a victory to Let’s Go Washington, the conservative group behind the measure, even as voters rejected two other initiatives it backed concerning parental rights and the repeal of the state’s tax on high earners.

Supporters argue that separating girls’ sports by biological sex protects fairness, safety and athletic opportunities for female students. Opponents contend the restrictions discriminate against transgender students and could subject girls to intrusive medical verification.

WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE

The dispute now extends beyond the election results.

Gender Justice League Executive Director Danni Askini told KUOW her organization was consulting partners and evaluating a possible challenge on student-privacy grounds. The group had not formally announced a lawsuit in that Nov. 5 report.

The ACLU of Washington also condemned the outcome, but told KUOW it does not discuss potential litigation. That response did not announce a lawsuit.

Washington Democrats, meanwhile, have said they support other organizations pursuing challenges but will not bring a case themselves.

"WA Dems will not be challenging the initiative in court. We believe there will be organizations who do and we support those efforts," the party previously told OutKick.

Party Chair Shasti Conrad called the initiative unconstitutional in a Nov. 5 statement.

The measure’s medical-verification requirement has become a central point of contention.

Its text requires a health examination and consent form, or another statement signed by a student’s personal healthcare provider, verifying biological sex as part of the required routine sports physical. That verification must rely on reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels. The text does not prescribe a particular examination or test.

Washington has allowed students to compete on teams consistent with their gender identity since 2007.

The debate also prompted protests from female athletes before the election. About a dozen Camas girls declined to race against a transgender teammate on Oct. 13, OutKick previously reported.

For schools, the immediate question is how to carry out the new requirements.

The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association told KUOW it was preparing changes for Dec. 3 and reviewing implementation, including physical-examination requirements. It said updated guidance and forms would go to schools after legal review.

item.title: Three high school football teams have their playoff fates decided by a midnight parking lot coin toss
item.description: Three Oklahoma high school football teams faced a midnight coin toss in a parking lot to decide which two would advance to the Class A-2 playoffs.
item.content:encoded:
In an ideal world, high school football playoff matchups are decided by on-the-field play. But sometimes, in reality, they are decided by a midnight coin toss in a parking lot in front of Catfish Roundup.

Three Oklahoma high school football teams – Liberty, Gore and Central Sallisaw – were all tied for third place in Class A-2, District 3. However, there were only four playoff spots, so only two of the teams could advance.

The problem? The Oklahoma Secondary School Activities Association’s (OSSAA) tiebreakers didn’t break any ties. The three teams had identical district records, split their head-to-head games and had the exact same point differential.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

So, the next best option? A midnight coin toss in the Catfish Roundup parking lot.

Central Sallisaw head coach Jeremy Thompson was in disbelief.

"Coin toss, is that really going to happen? I called Mr. Johnson and he confirmed it," Thompson said, according to 2News Oklahoma. "Yes, that's how it's going to go."

The coins were flipped, and Liberty and Central Sallisaw both flipped tails, ensuring they would move on to the playoffs.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I can't tell you I've ever flipped a point and been that nervous. It's a tough way to do it, but that's the way it is," Thompson said. "We're excited it went our way."

For Gore, there was no love in Oklahoma, as the coin did not flip their way. Gore head coach Nathan McCurley was gutted for his seniors.

"You just hate to see it for the seniors, especially how we've rallied these last four weeks to put ourselves in this position," McCurley said, according to 2News Oklahoma. "To have it go away on a coin flip, I'm not upset over that. It's just, I hate it for the kids more than anything."

For Liberty, on the other hand, the coin flipping the right way was a big deal for the school.

"You never know what's going to happen when you get in a situation like this, so it's a big deal for us, our school history," Liberty head coach Nate Green said, according to 2News Oklahoma. "We don't have a lot of trips to the playoffs."

Well, thanks to the coin, Liberty has an opportunity to play again and add to their school’s history.

item.title: STU BURGUIERE: Put your money where your mouth is: Prediction markets won the midterms
item.description: Billions of dollars in political advertising tried to mislead voters, but Kalshi's prediction markets had winners ahead in 98% of federal races.
item.content:encoded:
Billions of dollars were spent this election season to lie to you.

More than $12.8 billion was spent on political advertising in the 2026 midterms making this the most expensive election cycle in American history. In my home state of Texas, the Senate race drew preliminary estimates of nearly $573 million placing it among the most expensive non-presidential contests on record.

Despite all the differences between races and candidates, a few things were dependable. Every campaign said it was going to win. Every analyst said their numbers were right. Every super PAC said its candidate had the best policies and character. And the mainstream media picked its favorites, cut to commercial, and served up a dozen ads of warring politicians accusing each other of high crimes and misdemeanors.

TRADERS POUR NEARLY $1.3 BILLION INTO PREDICTING WHO WILL CONTROL CONGRESS

A massive industry exists to bend your view of reality toward whatever our would-be leaders in Washington and the state capitals want you to believe. Americans need a way to cut through that noise. No wonder prediction markets are booming.

As with any new technology, prediction markets have drawn a lot of attention and a lot of criticism. Senators wrote letters warning about election contracts. States moved to sue or ban them outright. And somewhere, a podcaster is still on hour 133 of explaining how it's all rigged.

POLLSTERS MISSED THE MARK AGAIN — BUT THIS TIME, IT WASN'T REPUBLICANS THEY UNDERESTIMATED

Then Election Day settled the argument. Across all tracked federal contests, Kalshi's markets had the eventual winner out front in 98% of races. The markets not only correctly priced non-competitive incumbents they also accurately reflected the razor-thin odds in core battlegrounds.

This wasn't a one-time fluke. Kalshi studied 2,243,741 of its resolved markets, dating from its launch in 2021 through mid-2026. It found that prices became remarkably well calibrated as events approached. In plain English, the prices meant what they said. Events priced at 30 cents happened about 30% of the time; events priced at 90 cents, about 90%.

Outside researchers have reached the same conclusion. Brier.fyi, an independent site that measures prediction-market accuracy, saw a similar pattern across nearly 74,000 Kalshi markets. In a study published last month in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, researchers examined more than 1 million resolved forecasts across four platforms and found events happened about as often as their prices said they would. A Washington Post review of this year's primaries showed that candidates won about as often as their market prices suggested.

THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS GETS A WALL STREET-STYLE SCOREBOARD POWERED BY REAL-MONEY BETS

Despite that long track record, critics will seize on upsets like Democrat Annie Andrews' defeat of Republican Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina as proof that prediction markets are worthless. The markets had her as the underdog, about a 1-in-3 shot heading into Election Day. But if underdogs never won, the markets wouldn't be working. Upsets like hers are exactly what a 1-in-3 price promises.

Prediction markets don't have to be perfect to be useful. They're an incredible addition to the polling, forecasting and reporting we already have, and they make all of it better.

Serious data journalism is expensive. As newsrooms have cut budgets and staff, the deep dives and data desks have been some of the first casualties. Prediction markets give that work a new reason to exist. When information is worth money, someone will pay for it. That means more research, more deep-dive reporting and more jobs for data nerds. That's a win for all of us. Reliable information has never been more valuable, and markets reward people for finding it, weighing it and acting on it.

LEE CARTER: THE 5 WORDS THAT EXPLAIN THIS ELECTION BETTER THAN ANY COMMERCIAL

Show me a profitable trader, and I'll show you someone who would rather read a precinct-by-precinct breakdown of Hinds County, Mississippi, than finish a Netflix series. Ask me how I know.

Understanding the world is no longer just something you can show off at cocktail parties. Now, your dedication to the truth can potentially improve your financial well-being and, at the same time, help make all of us better informed.

For anyone who has felt shut out by the mainstream media, prediction markets are especially good news. They're the next chapter in a long story.

MEMBERS OF CONGRESS USING ONLINE PREDICTION MARKETS? DON'T BET ON IT

For decades, three networks and a handful of anchors decided what it was acceptable to believe. Rush Limbaugh broke that hold on talk radio, giving millions of listeners an alternative. Fox News Channel followed with "We Report, You Decide." Blogs and podcasts offered additional perspectives and drew attention to stories that might have never been covered.

But with billions of dollars still lined up to twist the truth, we can always use a new way to separate fact from spin.

Prediction markets do that by making you put your money where your mouth is. A campaign insider can insist a race is in the bag with no downside. A trader has to back the same claim with cash. In a market, you only get paid for being right.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Even if you never trade, you benefit: Markets crystallize all available information into a single number, and that number has no reason to lie to you.

Depending on who you were rooting for, Tuesday was either exhilarating or devastating. On Election Day there are important issues at stake and emotions run high. That's exactly why it helps to have a way to set those feelings aside and see the race as clearly as possible.

In more than a decade of trading these markets, I've learned that the best traders share one habit: They don't invest with their hearts. I've been fortunate enough to come out ahead cycle after cycle, often in years when the results went against what I'd hoped. That's the discipline these markets teach (and require): It's forecasting, not wishcasting. We root for the world we want, but we invest in the world we have.

If investing in elections feels a little strange, consider this: Politicians have been making money off you for decades. Maybe it's time to return the favor.

item.title: Paris agitators defy police orders, renew nationwide protests centered in Paris
item.description: Videos and photos show tear gas and fires throughout Paris as 70,000 security forces deploy against France protests despite police bans on gatherings.
item.content:encoded:
Protesters in France are continuing to demonstrate in Paris and across the nation despite police prohibitions on gatherings in the capital.

The Paris Police Prefecture denied numerous formal requests for permits allowing protests in various areas of the city, citing October riots that led to thousands of arrests and violent clashes between protesters and law enforcement.

"These events demonstrated the intention of certain individuals to target the institutions of the Republic, specifically through actions directed against public buildings and State services in order to undermine the foundations of the Republic," the police wrote, according to a Fox News Digital translation of a police order.

"That these elements characterize a particular and serious risk to public institutions, agent safety, and the normal functioning of public services during such demonstrations," the statement continued.

FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC'

FRANCE DEPLOYS 70,000 POLICE OFFICERS TO PREPARE FOR NEW WAVE OF PROTESTS ON HALLOWEEN

Police also prohibited a rally of France's popular Yellow Vest protest movement scheduled for Place de la Concorde, citing security concerns.

Despite the ban, prominent Yellow Vest members attended and were arrested at the National Assembly in front of Place de la Concorde.

Benjamin Ball, a member of the Yellow Vests coordination group, and spokesperson Azelma Sigaux, were both arrested early in the afternoon Saturday, according to the Agence France-Presse (AFP).

PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE

France's Interior Ministry anticipated 170,000 people to protest nationwide Saturday, a day marking the fourth straight week of protests.

The country deployed 70,000 security forces to quell the demonstrations, according to the AFP.

"The risk is exactly the same as on previous Saturdays," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, instructing authorities "not to lower their guard," AFP reported.

LIMOGES TOWN HALL 'LARGELY LOST' AFTER FAR-LEFT RIOTERS SET HISTORIC BUILDING ON FIRE AMID FRENCH UNREST

Videos and photos showed French authorities deploying tear gas and detaining rioters while fires burned throughout Paris.

French authorities also report that protesters have lobbed projectiles at police.

Demonstrators are protesting high costs of living, among other things, as student and teacher unions join Yellow Vests at the mass rallies.

On Monday, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is due to meet with leaders from the unions to discuss wages and purchasing power, AFP reported.

Despite the planned tête-à-tête, union leaders are calling for fresh strikes on Tuesday to keep the pressure on the government, claiming the unions are "in a position of strength (and) the government in a position of weakness and starting to yield."

Since student and union protests began in mid-September, National Assembly Deputy Leader Marine Le Pen has surged in national polling and is now seen as likely to force a runoff in the presidential election after announcing her candidacy in October.

Fox News Digital contacted the French Interior Ministry and Paris Police Prefecture for further information.
