item.title: California DA says Gavin Newsom's 'cruel' death row clemency stabs crime victims 'in the heart'
item.description: Orange County DA Todd Spitzer criticized Gov. Gavin Newsom for commuting California's death row sentences to life without parole, calling the mass clemency "immoral."
item.content:encoded:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row, a move that Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer criticized as stabbing crime victims "in the heart."

Speaking on "Fox News @ Night," Spitzer took direct aim at Newsom, saying his decision is "immoral" and arguing that it disregards the extensive judicial review given to death penalty cases.

"He literally stabbed in the heart many victims who have suffered through an already-unjust justice system in California that already revictimizes victims over and over and over," Spitzer said.

NEWSOM’S DEATH-ROW COMMUTATIONS SPARK DA REVOLT AS PROSECUTORS WARN OF LEGAL FIGHT

Among the victims' relatives criticizing the decision is Marc Klaas, whose 12-year-old daughter, Polly, was kidnapped from her bedroom at knifepoint and murdered in 1993 by condemned killer Richard Allen Davis. Davis was sentenced to death in 1996, and the California Supreme Court upheld his conviction and sentence in 2009.

"Baby killers and cop killers and spree killers and serial killers have all found an ally in Gavin Newsom," Klaas told Fox News Digital in October.

MICHAEL RUIZ: CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS REVOLT AFTER NEWSOM ORDERS STATE'S WORST KILLERS OFF DEATH ROW

Newsom announced the plan for mass commutations in a letter on Nov. 5, in which he told Californians he would exercise his "constitutional clemency authority to commute all California death sentences to life without the possibility of parole."

The governor said he believes state-sanctioned killing is "incompatible with California's values" and argued that the death penalty cannot be applied fairly, pointing to the risk of executing innocent people.

GOP GOV DEWINE URGES OHIO TO ABOLISH THE DEATH PENALTY, SAYS IT IS NO LONGER A DETERRENT

Other death row inmates who could be affected by the commutations include Charles Ng, who was convicted of killing 11 people in the Sierra Nevada foothills, and Cary Stayner, who was convicted of murdering four people near Yosemite National Park in 1999 and was sentenced to death for three of the killings.

"Well, it was callous. It was calculated. It was mean. It was ugly. It was ill-spirited. It was [a] lack of any empathy. It was immoral," Spitzer said of Newsom's decision. "I could think of so many adjectives to describe the behavior of the cruel governor."

When reached for comment by Fox News Digital regarding Spitzer's criticisms, Newsom's office pointed to the governor's Nov. 5 letter announcing the commutations.

In the letter, Newsom acknowledged the emotional toll on grieving families, writing, "This decision is among the most difficult of my career, not because I doubt its necessity for our state but because I know its announcement may surface excruciating memories for victims' families."

CHARLES MANSON FOLLOWER TIED TO SHARON TATE MURDERS GETS RECOMMENDED FOR PAROLE AFTER 55 YEARS IN PRISON

Spitzer argued that converting death sentences to life without the possibility of parole (LWOP) could allow convicted killers to seek release if future changes to state law create a pathway to parole or resentencing.

"The legislature has tried to convert life without the possibility of parole to eligible for parole. So by converting death penalty to LWOP, it's actually L-WALK: walk out of prison," Spitzer said.

Gavin Newsom's office, however, says the commutations would not make the inmates eligible for release and that the sentences would remain life without the possibility of parole.

NEW YORK BILLS COULD ABOLISH LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE FOR SERIAL KILLERS AND COP KILLERS, CRITICS WARN

MENENDEZ BROTHERS GRANTED 2027 PAROLE HEARING A YEAR EARLIER THAN EXPECTED

Newsom's plan to commute 548 death sentences still faces a legal hurdle for hundreds of inmates. Under the California Constitution, commutations for inmates convicted of a felony on two or more occasions require a recommendation from the California Supreme Court with at least four justices concurring.

Still, Spitzer argued that Newsom's decision has already revictimized families by causing additional suffering after years of legal proceedings.

ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION

"Gavin Newsom says he can't sleep at night. He should never sleep at night with the revictimization that he has caused to these poor victims who have suffered irreparable harm," Spitzer said.

Fox News Digital’s Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

item.title: Bill Maher warns Democrats that some on far-left want 'communism' after midterm sweep
item.description: Bill Maher told his "Real Time" audience that far-left Democrats "want communism" and urged moderates to use their midterm wins to reclaim the party.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Bill Maher doubled down on his criticism of democratic socialists Friday, telling his "Real Time" audience that "these people want communism" and urging moderates to reclaim control of the party following Democrats' historic sweep in this week's midterm elections.

On Friday, Maher spoke with writer and podcast host Coleman Hughes regarding the rise of socialist policies within the Democratic Party — and the party’s apparent appetite for more moderate candidates — during the show’s roundtable discussion.

"My issues are high rents and crime," Hughes said. "Socialists don't tend to be good on those issues because they institute policies like rent control, which sound good and then end up increasing the rents in the long run."

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"And we got a hundred years of data on socialism," Hughes added. "It's not good for the economy. It's not a new idea."

Maher appeared to agree with his guest, arguing that many of the policies pushed by socialist candidates are more closely aligned with communist ideology.

LIBERAL HOT SPOT RESIDENTS CAN’T AGREE ON WHAT SOCIALISM MEANS AS FAR-LEFT MOVEMENTS GAINS STEAM

"We already have a lot of socialism and a lot of it is appropriate," Maher said. "That's not what these people are selling, these far-left people."

Maher said some government services and programs — including Medicare, the Marine Corps and Social Security — fall under his definition of socialism.

TRUMP'S CORPORATE STAKES ARE A GIFT TO THE NEXT DEMOCRATIC PRESIDENT

"It's anything the government does and the private sector doesn't," the comedian said. "You just read what they say in their manifesto. They want the government to take over everything. That is a prescription for failure."

Maher also argued that the sweeping victories by moderate Democrats could indicate a broader voter rejection of the policies advocated by far-left candidates.

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

"To me, one of the great results of this election was it gave moderates a big stick to beat them off with," Maher told his audience.

He added that moderate Democrats could use their midterm victories to regain control of the party, while suggesting that the socialist agenda may not be as popular with voters as its supporters believe.

JOE MANCHIN WARNS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE GAINING GROUND AS DEMOCRATS REMAIN SILENT

"Who has the guts to say this is the Democratic Party, you are doing a whole different thing," he continued. "We already have a lot of socialism, and I'm for most of it. We need most of it, but these people want communism."

BILL MAHER WARNS THAT THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IS BEING 'COLONIZED' BY SOCIALISTS, SAYS HIS 'VOTE IS IN PLAY'

The liberal comedian has repeatedly criticized the rise of socialism within the Democratic Party and warned about socialist policies ahead of the midterms earlier this year.

"I did say that it was about two months ago, and you see how quickly the news changes in just two months, because that was before the Supreme Court made a ruling on voting rights," Maher said at an event in June, referencing the Supreme Court's April 29 decision in "Louisiana v. Callais," which found that Louisiana's revised congressional map constituted an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.

"So, that has changed just in the last two months, and then the Democrats just elected three very far-left democratic socialists in New York who are crazy — like outright really crazy — so like, how are they gonna blow it? I don't know, but they seem to be well on their way," he added at the time.

Maher’s comments come after Democrats have won at least 254 U.S. House of Representatives races, according to the Associated Press — subsequently giving the party its largest House majority since 2009.

MAJORITY OF AMERICANS BROADLY REJECT SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY EVEN AS FAR LEFT SURGES TO POWER

Additionally, democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass earlier this week, becoming another democratic socialist elected to lead a major American city, following New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's victory last year.

However, Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital that Maher's criticisms of socialist policies — and his characterization of candidates who support them — are misguided as the comedian continues to criticize Democrats.

"There is something perfectly ‘Bill Maher’ about declaring it an ‘indictment of our educational system’ that young people supposedly do not understand socialism, and then immediately revealing that he does not understand it either," Shroff said. "Medicare and Social Security are social insurance programs. The Marine Corps is literally a branch of the military."

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

"If every service the government provides counts as socialism, then courts, cops and Congress are socialist too and the word has basically lost all meaning," he added. "He is mocking other people for being uneducated on the subject while demonstrating the same sloppy understanding himself."

Shroff also pointed to Maher's history of dining with President Donald Trump at the White House — most recently last month — and accused the liberal comedian of criticizing socialist policies more harshly when Democrats embrace them.

"And if Maher really wants to worry about socialism, he might want to look a little harder at his dinner buddy Donald Trump," Shroff said. "Trump’s government has taken roughly a 10 percent stake in Intel and about a 15 percent stake in MP Materials. Those examples are far closer to socialism than Medicare is. Yet somehow Maher’s socialism panic gets a lot quieter when Trump is the one doing it."

Fox News Digital reached out to Maher for comment.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.
